s1.syndrome_frame: Chronic multisystem disorder with erythrocytosis, cutaneous telangiectasias, and progressive intrapulmonary shunting
salient_findings: Scattered telangiectasias on the chest and back
key_facts: Dyspnea developed a few months after presentation
Telangiectasias appeared on the chest in 2012
Patient had clubbing with oxygen saturation of 90% to 92%
IgG κ monoclonal protein levels were 910 mg/dL
Patient had purple angiomatous papules on the lips resembling venous lakes

shortlist.label: Osler-Weber-Rendu Syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: similar to Hereditary Hemorrhagic Telangiectasia, with telangiectasias and shunting

shortlist.label: Hepatopulmonary Syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: intrapulmonary shunting and potential liver involvement

raw.rationale: The combination of erythrocytosis, elevated IgG κ monoclonal protein levels, and the presence of telangiectasias with classic spider angioma morphology, along with the development of dyspnea and increased intrapulmonary shunting, are consistent with POEMS Syndrome, which is characterized by polyneuropathy, organomegaly, endocrinopathy, monoclonal gammopathy, and skin changes.

rejected.label: Hereditary Hemorrhagic Telangiectasia
rejected.why: While it involves telangiectasias, the presence of monoclonal protein and erythrocytosis are not typical features of this condition

rejected.label: Osler-Weber-Rendu Syndrome
rejected.why: This is another term for Hereditary Hemorrhagic Telangiectasia and does not account for the monoclonal protein or erythrocytosis

rejected.label: Polycythemia Vera
rejected.why: Although it can cause erythrocytosis, it does not typically present with telangiectasias or monoclonal protein elevations

rejected.label: Hepatopulmonary Syndrome
rejected.why: This condition involves liver disease and intrapulmonary shunting but does not account for the monoclonal protein or the specific skin findings
